questions.question: Who must provide emergency response information?
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must give emergency response information to drivers.

questions.question: Who is responsible for putting placards on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: The shipper provides the placards. The driver must actually place them on the vehicle.

questions.question: To drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, you must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a commercial driver license with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any size vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying hazardous materials at that moment.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
The amount of packaging required for shipping.
The location on the trailer where items go.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class describes the risks it poses.

questions.question: Placarded vehicles must carry fire extinguishers rated at least:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's engine area must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: While driving, shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in a place you can easily reach while wearing your seat belt. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify that:

options.text: The package does not contain hazardous materials.
The package was prepared following all rules.
The package was packed at a specific location.
The package will be placed on the trailer first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The package was prepared following all rules.
questions.explanation: When shippers package hazardous materials, they confirm the package meets all required rules.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how are they told apart?

options.text: Non-hazardous materials are written in pencil.
Hazardous materials are written in red ink.

questions.explanation: On a shipping paper with both types of materials, hazardous materials must be identified by being listed first, highlighted in a different color, or marked with an "X" in a column labeled "HM."

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Some explosive or flammable materials cannot be loaded in cargo spaces with heaters.

questions.question: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be:

options.text: Inside a gas station looking through a window.
In the vehicle, awake or asleep.

questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it. They must know the hazards, know what to do in an emergency, and be able to move the vehicle if needed.

questions.question: If the letter "G" appears in Column 1 of a hazardous materials shipping paper, what else must be included?

options.text: The technical name of the hazardous material.
The type of packaging holding the hazardous material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The technical name of the hazardous material.
questions.explanation: A "G" in Column 1 means the material has a generic name. You must also include the technical name.

questions.question: When must a driver take the HazMat knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You must pass the HazMat knowledge test and pass a federal background check before renewing your CDL.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, how should they be listed?

options.text: Hazardous materials must be listed first.
Hazardous materials must be written larger.
Hazardous materials must be listed in red ink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazardous materials must be listed first.
questions.explanation: On shipping papers with both types of materials, hazardous materials must always be listed first.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with empty hazardous materials tanks, what must you do at railroad crossings?

options.text: You can cross without slowing or stopping.
You must slow down but don't need to stop.
You should never drive over railroad tracks.

questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings before crossing, even if the tanks are empty.

questions.question: If you have a collision while transporting Class 1 explosives, what should you do?

options.text: Do not warn others of the danger.
Keep the explosives in the vehicle until after separating the vehicles.
Remove the explosives before separating the vehicles involved.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the explosives before separating the vehicles involved.
questions.explanation: Warn others of the danger and keep bystanders away. Do not allow smoking or open fires. Remove all explosives and place them at least 200 feet away from the vehicles and buildings.

questions.question: Who is responsible for properly labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials properly. The driver should verify the materials are labeled correctly.

questions.question: Which agency performs a background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: You must pass a Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background check to get or renew a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: How should you label a hazardous material item that is too small for the label?

options.text: Tie it with other hazardous materials and label the bundle with paper on the outside.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box displaying a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: Hazard warning labels must be diamond-shaped. If the label will not fit on the package, attach it to a tag securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What should you do with the engine when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver refuel it.

questions.explanation: Always turn the engine off before refueling. Someone must always be at the nozzle watching the fuel flow.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual has all the information needed to pass the test, but not all the information needed to do the job safely. Attend hazardous materials training courses to learn more.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Keep liquid discharge valves closed except during loading and unloading.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Load hazardous materials away from heat.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake before loading. Keep hazardous materials away from heat. Do not use hooks or tools that could damage containers or packaging.

questions.question: The National Response Center must be notified of an incident resulting in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Report incidents involving death or hospitalization to the National Response Center. Also report incidents with $50,000 or more in property damage, public evacuation, closure of a major route for more than one hour, or suspected contamination with radiation, bacteria, or toxins.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class tell you?

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
How quickly the material must reach its destination.
The country of origin of the material.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class shows what risks it poses.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual has all information needed to pass the written exam. However, to do the job safely, you need more information. Attend hazardous materials training courses to learn more.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
Attach a scannable QR code instead.
Reduce the label size to fit on the package.
Paste the label on the trailer wall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a label will not fit on the package, place it on a tag that is securely attached to the package.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in the trailer, how should it be cleaned?
questions.explanation: Thoroughly wash all parts of the vehicle exposed to corrosive materials with water.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting packages with radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation spreads from the package and passes through to other packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads from the package and passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from each radioactive package and passes through nearby packages. The number of packages that can be loaded together is controlled.

questions.question: How must containers of hazardous materials be loaded?

options.text: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braced to prevent movement during transportation.
questions.explanation: Brace containers so they cannot fall, slide, or bounce during transportation. All hazardous materials packages must be secured.

questions.question: If hazardous materials are leaking and the driver has no phone, what should they do?

options.text: Drive to a phone to alert emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials clean-up facility.

questions.explanation: If hazardous materials leak, do not move the vehicle more than necessary. Driving spreads contamination. Instead, park safely, secure the vehicle, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you have no phone, send someone else to get help.
